group.title: Describing places
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: Covered with sand.
examples: The children played on the {sandy} beach all day.
wrong: The sandy beach was covered with big rocks and no sand at all.

words.meaning: Full of people, energy and things happening.
examples: The square is {lively} at night, with music and cafes.
wrong: The lively town was silent, and nobody was out.

words.meaning: Not modern; from an earlier time.
examples: My grandma’s kitchen is {old-fashioned}, with an old wooden stove.
wrong: The old-fashioned office was full of the newest computers.

words.meaning: Level, with no hills or high parts.
examples: The land here is {flat}, so cycling is easy.
wrong: The town is very flat, with steep hills on every street.

words.meaning: Large from one side to the other.
examples: The road is {wide} enough for four cars.
wrong: The street is so wide that two people can’t walk side by side.

words.meaning: Covered with or full of rocks.
examples: Wear good shoes; the path is {rocky}.
wrong: The rocky field was soft grass with not one stone in it.

words.meaning: Liked by a lot of people.
examples: This park is {popular} with families on Sundays.
wrong: The cafe is very popular, so it is always empty.

words.meaning: Of or in the area near you.
examples: We buy bread at the {local} bakery on our street.
wrong: The local shop is in another country.

words.meaning: Full of tourists and things made for them.
examples: The old town is very {touristy}, with souvenir shops everywhere.
wrong: The touristy street had no visitors, no hotels and no gift shops.

words.meaning: Connected with the past or with history.
examples: The town has many {historical} buildings from the 1600s.
wrong: The historical buildings were all built last month.

words.meaning: Very surprising and very good.
examples: The view from the tower was {amazing}.
wrong: The hotel was amazing, so we left after one night and asked for our money back.

words.meaning: Having a bad smell.
examples: The fish market is a bit {smelly} in the afternoon.
wrong: The smelly garden was full of sweet, fresh air.

words.meaning: Full of light.
examples: Our kitchen is {bright} because it has big windows.
wrong: The bright room had no windows and no lamps.

words.meaning: Known by many people.
examples: It’s a {well-known} restaurant; everyone in town has been there.
wrong: The well-known shop is a secret that no one knows about.

words.meaning: The shape of a city’s buildings against the sky.
examples: The city {skyline} looks beautiful at night with all the lights.
wrong: The skyline is the floor under a city’s streets.

words.meaning: Very beautiful, big and impressive.
examples: The palace has a {magnificent} garden with huge fountains.
wrong: The magnificent castle was a small, ugly shed.

words.meaning: Far away from towns and other people.
examples: They live on a {remote} farm, two hours from the nearest shop.
wrong: Their remote house is right in the city center.

words.meaning: With many factories.
examples: It’s an {industrial} town with big factories by the river.
wrong: The industrial area has only fields and cows.

words.meaning: Not far away.
examples: We swim at a {nearby} lake, just five minutes away.
wrong: The nearby station is a three-hour drive away.

words.meaning: In or near the middle of a place.
examples: Our hotel was very {central}, close to all the sights.
wrong: The central hotel is far outside the city.

words.meaning: With a lot of trees and plants.
examples: They live in a {leafy} street with big trees on both sides.
wrong: The leafy area has no trees or plants at all.

words.meaning: Very full of people.
examples: The train was {packed}, so we had to stand.
wrong: The packed bus had only two people on it.

words.meaning: With no people in it.
examples: At 3 a.m. the streets were {deserted}.
wrong: The deserted beach was full of people.

words.meaning: Popular and modern at the moment.
examples: It’s a {fashionable} area with new bars and shops.
wrong: The fashionable cafe is one nobody wants to visit.

words.meaning: Land outside towns, with fields, farms and trees.
examples: We like walking in the {countryside} on weekends.
wrong: The countryside is full of tall office buildings and traffic.

words.meaning: The most important city of a country, where the government is.
examples: Tokyo is the {capital} of Japan.
wrong: The capital is a small village where nobody important lives.

words.meaning: A part of a town, country or place.
examples: We live in a quiet {area} near the park.
wrong: An area is a kind of food you cook in the oven.

words.meaning: A large part of a country.
examples: This {region} is famous for its wine.
wrong: A region is a small room in a house.

words.meaning: The place where something is.
examples: The hotel is in a great {location}, near the beach.
wrong: The location of the hotel is the price of a room.

words.meaning: The town or city where you were born or grew up.
examples: I go back to my {hometown} every summer to see my parents.
wrong: My hometown is a city I visited once on holiday.

words.meaning: An interesting place that tourists visit.
examples: We saw all the main {sights} of Rome in two days.
wrong: The sights of a city are the places no one wants to see.

words.meaning: The main, middle part of a city.
examples: The {city center} has the best shops and restaurants.
wrong: We left the city center and drove into the middle of the town.

words.meaning: A long way from here.
examples: My parents live {far away}, so I only visit once a year.
wrong: The shop is far away, just next door.

words.meaning: In a place far from any towns or people.
examples: The hotel is {in the middle of nowhere}, miles from any town.
wrong: Their flat is in the middle of nowhere, right next to the main station.

words.meaning: Inside a building.
examples: There’s an {indoor} pool, so you can swim when it rains.
wrong: The indoor market is under the open sky.

words.meaning: Outside, not in a building.
examples: The hotel has an {outdoor} pool in the garden.
wrong: We sat at an outdoor table inside the restaurant.

words.meaning: Dangerous; not safe.
examples: The old bridge is {unsafe}, so it’s closed.
wrong: The park is unsafe, so it’s a good place for small children at night.

words.meaning: Covered with dry dirt.
examples: The road to the village is {dusty} in summer.
wrong: The dusty shelf was perfectly clean.

words.meaning: The part of a town next to a river, lake or the sea.
examples: We walked along the {waterfront} and watched the boats.
wrong: The waterfront is the part of town far from any water.

words.meaning: With a lot of hills.
examples: San Francisco is very {hilly}, so walking is hard work.
wrong: The town is hilly, with land as flat as a table.
